chapter: New Orleans bands, clubs and players
title: George Lewis's and Gorman's ideas about playing softer and slower
summary: He agrees that bands should play more softly and slowly, dislikes Preservation Hall loudness, and recalls Gorman's planned band.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You know when we went to see him on Saturday to visit him after the flood and everything, he was talking about his ideas about music. Do you agree with him at all?

I think that the way he's, like he said, we should play more soft and we should play more slow. I think that is right. Gorman told me the same thing. When I was always, he told me exactly the same thing. When the clarinet play in low reggae, the band should, so they should play not too loud. I don't like the way they play at the Preservation Hall. There's tunes and drums, solas, bass, band, and so it's all the time. It's awful boring.
What about Gorman now? He was organizing a band just before he died.
Yeah, he told me he was organizing a band. He also told me who was in the band. But I can't remember it. I only remember Andy Anderson.
I saw Anderson Sunday and I asked him about it, but we didn't have time. The band's time was not.
I asked him too, later on. And he told me it was right that he had a band. But since the hurricane, he hadn't heard anything from Gorman.
I think he told me they had three or four rehearsals. Yeah.

Well Gorman told me he was going to try to get the band out in the country and play, because he knows some places like, outside of New Orleans, where he could get out. But he was very enthusiastic about it. I don't think he would turn out so good. He would think it would make a hit or something.
